items_missed: Set Agenda: never asked "how are you today," and never gave a real agenda statement (what we'll cover + rough time) with an explicit "sound good?" confirmation — jumped straight to building the profile.
Probe: no additional-rooms question (garage/storage/balcony), no narrow-hallway/tight-turn access question, no elevator/parking/HOA access check, no moving-stressors question.

Estimate: no stairs/elevator variable mentioned, no specialty-items (piano/safe/antiques) tie-in to the time range, and no walk-distance or equivalents (e.g. school-bus reference) used to explain why the estimate could move.
Save Your Ass: entire section skipped — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no "take a carload" tip, no close-out check.

Quote/Booking: didn't attempt to lock in Sunday or Monday on the call, never said "no deposit required," didn't mention a bolded detail list at the top of the email, didn't frame the callback as "reply with any corrections," and never asked "any other questions before I let you go?"
Bonus: rapport stayed one-directional (rep's own enthusiasm - "Oh, that's awesome") rather than a genuine back-and-forth moment with the customer.
top_strength: The pricing and differentiators walkthrough is excellent and complete: hourly rate, what's included, trip-fee rule, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, No Worries damage coverage, and the full no-hidden-fees pitch all landed cleanly in one organized pass, and he even caught his own initial 2,400 sq ft guess with a live Zillow-style check and said out loud "I might say five guys" once he saw the home was actually 5,000 sq ft.
coaching_note: Your pricing explanation is genuinely a model call for that section - keep doing it exactly like this. The gap is Save Your Ass: it's a zero on this call, and it's the section that saves customers money, so build it into your close every time, even on a chaotic call like this one. Also tighten the finish - you never asked "any other questions before I let you go," never said "no deposit required," and never tried to lock in Sunday or Monday even loosely. And when you catch a mismatch like the 5,000 sq ft home versus your 2,400 sq ft guess, say the new total dollar number out loud instead of just noting the crew change - Chloe left the call not knowing the real price.
phone_presence_notes: Consistent warmth and patience with a scattered caller ("no worries" repeated genuinely, offered his personal cell unprompted, used Chloe's name three times, warm close), though the long pricing recitation ran fairly scripted.
